**Snowflake Inc. (CIK 1640147) — Notable operational changes, acquisitions and restructuring in fiscal 2025 (year ended January 31, 2025)**

Source: Form 10-K for FY2025, filed March 21, 2025 (local file snow-20250131.htm).

**1. Acquisitions (three business combinations in FY2025)**
- **Datavolo, Inc.** — acquired all outstanding capital stock on **November 25, 2024**. Datavolo was a privately held company that built dataflow infrastructure for creating, managing and observing multimodal data pipelines for enterprise AI; Snowflake acquired it for its developed technology and talent. Preliminary purchase consideration was **$106.8 million**, comprising ~0.5 million Class A shares valued at **$87.7 million** (at $171.42/share) and **$19.1 million in cash**. Allocation included $65.9 million goodwill, a $35.0 million developed-technology intangible (5-year life), $5.9 million cash and $7.7 million short-term investments acquired. Separately, ~0.4 million shares worth **$64.6 million** were issued to certain Datavolo employees and are being expensed as post-combination stock-based compensation over four years. (chunks 467200, 468800, 283200)
- **Two other privately held companies** — acquired during FY2025 for an aggregate **$19.2 million in cash**, recorded as business combinations, with $14.8 million goodwill, $4.4 million customer-relationships and $4.1 million developed-technology intangibles. (chunk 470400)
- Total cash paid for business combinations, net of cash acquired, was **$30.3 million** in FY2025 versus $275.7 million in FY2024. (chunk 390400)

**2. Restructuring**
- Snowflake incurred costs under a **restructuring plan for a majority-owned subsidiary** during FY2025: **$7.7 million** charged to cost of product revenue and **$11.0 million** charged to research and development (about $18.7 million in total across those two lines). The filing does not describe the specific actions (e.g., headcount) of that plan in the excerpts reviewed. (chunks 328000, 332800)

**3. Facility/real-estate changes**
- In **November 2024** the company signed an agreement for a new office facility in **Menlo Park, California**, and it began exiting its **San Mateo** office, with relocation expected to be completed by April 2025. Management expects **general and administrative expenses to increase in fiscal 2026 due to anticipated asset impairment charges upon the cease-use of the San Mateo facility**. (chunks 262400, 316800)

**4. Management/leadership changes**
- **February 2024:** Frank Slootman retired as CEO and **Sridhar Ramaswamy** was appointed CEO (Slootman remained Chairman of the Board).
- **July 2024:** Grzegorz Czajkowski, EVP Engineering and Support, resigned; **Vivek Raghunathan** was appointed SVP, Engineering and Support in **September 2024**.
- **February 2025** (subsequent to year-end): CFO **Michael P. Scarpelli** notified the company of his intention to retire. (chunk 147200)

**5. Other capital/operational items**
- Headcount rose to **2,257** at January 31, 2025 from 2,002 a year earlier. (chunk 332800)
- The company issued **$2.3 billion** of convertible senior notes in FY2025 and repurchased **$1.93 billion** of common stock, with $2.0 billion remaining available under the repurchase program. (chunks 390400, 283200)

**Limitation:** The above is drawn from the FY2025 10-K text; the specific mechanics of the majority-owned-subsidiary restructuring (scope, headcount, completion) are not detailed in the passages retrieved, and the San Mateo impairment is a stated expectation for fiscal 2026, not a charge recognized in fiscal 2025.
